chores.intro: Add a job, say how heavy it is and how often it comes round. The app hands them out on its own, keeps the load even, and shows its working.

fields.name: Chore name
fields.what: The job itself, written the way you'd say it out loud. You can't add two that are identical - same name, same effort, same frequency - because afterwards nobody could tell them apart.

fields.name: Effort
fields.what: How heavy the job is, from 1 to 10. The word next to the box tells you where you've landed: 1-2 easy, 3-4 moderate, 5-7 hard, 8-9 very hard, 10 the worst job.
fields.example: 2 for the bins, 10 for the bathroom

fields.name: How often
fields.what: How long each turn lasts - and how much the job counts. A daily chore gets done seven times a week, so it is worth seven times a weekly one of the same effort. Turns end at midnight, your midnight.
fields.example: Daily for the dishes, weekly for the bathroom

fields.name: The date box
fields.what: Which day you are looking at. A chore shows on every day of its turn, so a weekly job appears all week - the row tells you the day it is actually due by. Pick a future day to see what is coming; you cannot tick anything off there.

fields.name: The three dropdowns
fields.what: Who, what state, and how often - and they stack. Leave them alone to see your own chores for today, or combine them to ask something narrower.

fields.name: Daily chores / Weekly chores
fields.what: How far through the current round you are, with one box per kind of chore. '4 of 13 done' in the daily box means that of the jobs that come back every day, you have finished 4 effort out of 13. A weekly job is counted in the weekly box only, never in the daily one - so an empty daily box does not mean you have nothing on. Each box fills up, turns green when you are finished, then empties and starts again next round.

fields.name: Mark done
fields.what: Ticks the job off and credits you its effort. Only the person holding it can press it. Forgot at the time? Change the date box back to that day and tick it there - it still counts.
fields.example: Press it when the bins are out

fields.name: Swap this
fields.what: Offers your chore to one person or to the whole group. Credit follows whoever actually does it, so trading costs neither of you anything. You will be told whether they said yes or no.

fields.name: Missed
fields.what: A turn whose time ran out before it was done. You lose that credit, which drops you down the order, so the app sends you more work. That particular chore also skips you next time, so it gets done by somebody. Click the number to see which jobs, and go tick any you actually did.

fields.name: Total finished since the group started
fields.what: Every chore each person has ever completed - daily, weekly, biweekly and monthly all added together - going right back to the day the group started. It is shown as an average week so that a daily job and a monthly one can be compared fairly: 99 means they average about 99 effort a week, not that they did 99 this week. It never empties, and it is the number the app uses to decide who gets the next chore. The boxes above are about the round you are in right now; this one is the long-run record.

fields.name: Show the math
fields.what: Why that person got that chore: what it is worth, how often it comes round, where everyone stood at the time, and the margin that decided it. Open it when a split looks wrong.

fields.name: Rotate now
fields.what: You should not need it. Turns are handed out automatically when you open the app, and again overnight. The button is only there to force it.

ious.intro: For money lent outside any shared bill — cash you handed over.

fields.name: I lent
fields.what: Who you gave the money to. You're always the lender here.

fields.name: Amount
fields.what: How much you handed over. The buttons are the notes your currency actually has.

fields.name: Note
fields.what: What it was for, so nobody has to remember in a month. Optional.

fields.name: Category
fields.what: Groups it for the monthly recap. Optional.

expenses.intro: A bill somebody paid that the group is sharing.

fields.name: Title
fields.what: What the money went on.

fields.name: Amount
fields.what: The total on the receipt, before splitting.

fields.name: Paid by
fields.what: Whoever actually handed over the money. They get paid back by everyone else.

fields.name: Split between
fields.what: Everyone who shared it. The total divides evenly between the people ticked — leave someone out and they owe nothing.

fields.name: Share
fields.what: Adds someone with no Reckon account as a guest. They count as one more head in the split, and you pick who covers them if they don't pay.
fields.example: A friend who came to dinner

availability.intro: Mark when you're free so the group can find a time that suits everyone.

fields.name: The grid
fields.what: Drag across it to mark yourself free. Drag again over your own bar to remove it.

fields.name: Repeats weekly
fields.what: Turn on before dragging if you're free at that time every week, not just once.

fields.name: The bright patches
fields.what: Where everyone's free time overlaps. The brighter it is, the more people can make it.

proposals.intro: Suggest a plan and let everyone say whether they can make it.

fields.name: Title
fields.what: What you're suggesting.

fields.name: Cost per person
fields.what: Roughly what it'll cost each person. Anyone whose budget is lower gets a quiet flag. Optional.

fields.name: Covers
fields.what: Which dietary needs it suits. People it doesn't suit get flagged. Optional.

fields.name: Location
fields.what: Coordinates, used to work out travel for everyone. Optional.
